lines.text: How long is a chain of us? Everyone on Earth, holding hands.
lines.phonemes: hˌaʊ lˈɔŋ ɪz ɐ tʃˈeɪn ʌv ˌʌs? ˈɛvɹɪwˌʌn ˌɔn ˈɜːθ, hˈoʊldɪŋ hˈændz.

lines.text: Stretch your arms out wide. You are about as wide as you are tall. Call it a meter and a half, for grown-ups and kids together.
lines.phonemes: stɹˈɛtʃ jʊɹ ˈɑːɹmz ˈaʊt wˈaɪd. juː ɑːɹ ɐbˌaʊt æz wˈaɪd æz juː ɑːɹ tˈɔːl. kˈɔːl ɪɾ ɐ mˈiːɾɚ ænd ɐ hˈæf, fɔːɹ ɡɹˈoʊnˌʌps ænd kˈɪdz təɡˈɛðɚ.

lines.text: Now add all eight billion people, one after another, hand in hand. Out past the horizon it goes, until the line is about twelve million kilometers long.
lines.phonemes: nˈaʊ ˈæd ˈɔːl ˈeɪt bˈɪliən pˈiːpəl, wˈʌn ˈæftɚɹ ɐnˈʌðɚ, hˈænd ɪn hˈænd. ˈaʊt pˈæst ðə hɚɹˈaɪzən ɪt ɡˈoʊz, ʌntˈɪl ðə lˈaɪn ɪz ɐbˌaʊt twˈɛlv mˈɪliən kɪlˈɑːmɪɾɚz lˈɔŋ.

lines.text: That number is too big to picture. So let's wrap the line around something we all know: the Earth. Pull it tight, like a thread.
lines.phonemes: ðæt nˈʌmbɚɹ ɪz tˈuː bˈɪɡ tə pˈɪktʃɚ. sˌoʊ lˈɛts ɹˈæp ðə lˈaɪn ɚɹˈaʊnd sˈʌmθɪŋ wiː ˈɔːl nˈoʊ: ðɪ ˈɜːθ. pˈʊl ɪt tˈaɪt, lˈaɪk ɐ θɹˈɛd.

lines.text: It circles the Earth about three hundred and ten times. And one lap needs only about one person in three hundred of us.
lines.phonemes: ɪt sˈɜːkəlz ðɪ ˈɜːθ ɐbˌaʊt θɹˈiː hˈʌndɹɪd ænd tˈɛn tˈaɪmz. ænd wˈʌn lˈæp nˈiːdz ˈoʊnli ɐbˌaʊt wˈʌn pˈɜːsən ɪn θɹˈiː hˈʌndɹɪd ʌv ˌʌs.

lines.text: Make everyone a little shorter or taller, and the chain still wraps the Earth hundreds of times.
lines.phonemes: mˌeɪk ˈɛvɹɪwˌʌn ɐ lˈɪɾəl ʃˈɔːɹɾɚ ɔːɹ tˈɔːlɚ, ænd ðə tʃˈeɪn stˈɪl ɹˈæps ðɪ ˈɜːθ hˈʌndɹɪdz ʌv tˈaɪmz.

lines.text: The same line would reach the Moon again and again. We are each small, but together we are very long.
lines.phonemes: ðə sˈeɪm lˈaɪn wʊd ɹˈiːtʃ ðə mˈuːn ɐɡˈɛn ænd ɐɡˈɛn. wiː ɑːɹ ˈiːtʃ smˈɔːl, bˌʌt təɡˌɛðɚ wiː ɑːɹ vˈɛɹi lˈɔŋ.

lines.text: Next envelope: a rope round the Earth, lifted one meter.
lines.phonemes: nˈɛkst ˈɑːnvəlˌoʊp: ɐ ɹˈoʊp ɹˈaʊnd ðɪ ˈɜːθ, lˈɪftᵻd wˈʌn mˈiːɾɚ.
